approach: Reuse the scope guard's line grouping (group_lines, line_attempts) for every part. (1) scope_guard.rs gains a pure summary of each line (attempt count, count of attempts that did not land = Rejected or Failed, Environment excluded, landed flag, state, diagnosis mark) and Athena::line_summaries / line_summary / line_of built on group_lines. The constant DIAGNOSE_AFTER = 2 is the threshold. (2) Job (athena.job/1) gains `line: Option<String>` (serde default, skipped when None, so old records load); run/mod.rs dispatch fills it from line_of. (3) A new core module diagnosis.rs holds the diagnosis mark (a file under <state>/scope/<first id>.diagnosis.json, created with create_new so a line is claimed once) and Athena::diagnose_line. diagnose_line runs the new Diagnosis role once over the line's attempts, validates the output, commits the invocation record and exactly one follow-up request on the steward channel, then completes the mark with the follow-up job id and the reasoning. A role failure or invalid output keeps the claim, marks it failed and queues nothing, so spend is bounded; the operator deletes the file to ask again, as for a pause. (4) athena-context gets prompts/diagnosis.md, DIAGNOSIS_FRAME, brief builder, DiagnosisOutput with schema and a pure check() (every failed attempt has one of five categories, exactly one follow-up of four kinds, non-empty reasoning). The frame is composed with the contract only and checked against the verifier's budget set, as the critic is, so no shared prompt changes. (5) The drain gets Steps::line_standing, diagnose and diagnose_cap (defaults: no standing, so every existing Steps impl and test is unchanged) and a helper Drain::diagnosis_end called at the top of each attempt and at the failures >= ATTEMPTS exit, before the paused and flagged checks. It returns the new ItemEnd::Diagnosed, which is passed over. A diagnosed line is never diagnosed again, and only its own follow-up item may run, and only while no attempt has failed since the diagnosis. (6) status.rs adds StatusView.open_lines and display.rs prints them. (7) Role::Diagnosis is added in athena-data, with the exhaustive fake-driver arms. CHANGELOG gets four entries.

decisions.choice: Count only Rejected and Failed attempts toward the threshold (new pub fn failed_attempts in scope_guard.rs, documented as excluding Environment); threshold is the constant DIAGNOSE_AFTER = 2, not configuration.
decisions.reason: The scope guard already classifies stops through verdict_of and StopCause (scope_guard.rs:544-556) and its counted() drops Environment. The brief says the rule is code, and athena.toml is not to change.

rejected.why: It resets every run and counts environment failures. A later drain run would retry a line that already failed twice.

decisions.choice: Decide from the records by calling group_lines through Athena::line_summary; the drain asks it through a new Steps::line_standing, not by building its own groups.
decisions.reason: One grouping implementation. The records survive restarts, so the rule holds when the drain runs again. The Steps default of None keeps all existing drain tests and fakes unchanged.

rejected.option: Read Job.line in the drain and group by that string
rejected.why: A line recorded at dispatch can be stale: a re-ask text link can appear later. Old jobs have no value, and backfilling is out of scope. The field is for display and records.

rejected.option: Add the check to Steps::paused or flagged
rejected.why: Those mean a scope-guard signal. Diagnosis must also run when T1 or T4 already flagged or paused the line, which is the usual case at two failures, so it runs first.

decisions.choice: Store the line on Job (athena.job/1) as `line: Option<String>` with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")], written at dispatch in run/mod.rs from Athena::line_of (the first request id of the group containing the job).
decisions.reason: The reading says a job record. Job is built in one production place (run/mod.rs:1201), whereas Request has about 20 struct-literal sites. Job already has a default-skipped optional field (`pin`, `dispatch_branch`) as the pattern for loading old records.

rejected.why: Needs a change at every Request constructor, including steward, hestia and reading, which the brief does not list. The line is also not known until retries are linked.
Needs new store.rs routing and an AnyRecord variant for one string.

decisions.choice: Keep the diagnosis claim and mark in the state directory next to the pause and flag marks (scope/<first>.diagnosis.json, create_new), with the full reasoning also carried in the committed follow-up request text and the committed invocation record.
decisions.reason: There is precedent in scope_guard.rs (pause_path, flag_path, write_mark). create_new gives an atomic once-per-line claim even with concurrent drain workers, with no new record type. Failed diagnosis bounded to one spend.

rejected.why: Larger change (AnyRecord, store.rs, check_record_file, canonical path) for the same effect. Can be added later.

rejected.option: Re-run a failed diagnosis automatically on the next drain
rejected.why: Unbounded model spend on the very lines that already wasted money.

decisions.choice: Run the diagnosis inside the drain through Steps::diagnose, holding diagnose_cap against the budget as check_page does (drain.rs:2423-2438). If the cap does not fit, end the item as ItemEnd::Budget without claiming the line.
decisions.reason: Matches the existing pattern for model calls made by the drain, and keeps the diagnosis within the budget the user set.

rejected.option: Queue the diagnosis as a request for a later pass
rejected.why: Needs a new job kind that the reader and producer pipeline cannot run. Nothing would execute it.

decisions.choice: Add Role::Diagnosis in athena-data. The invocation record is filed under the line's last job id, with the next free seq, and the run borrows the verifier's model and budget, as the steward does.
decisions.reason: The invocation needs a role. Filing it under an existing job needs no new Records vector in store.rs, and the spend then shows on the line.

rejected.why: It would be counted as steward runs (store.rs:422) and confuse steward and Hestia tallies.

rejected.option: Add a diagnosis_runs vector like steward_runs
rejected.why: Extra store.rs change not needed for the goal.

decisions.choice: Frame composed from CONTRACT plus DIAGNOSIS_FRAME only, checked against BudgetSet::Verifier (as CRITIC_FRAME is); no new BudgetSet and no change to contract.md, reader.md or verifier.md.
decisions.reason: The contract has 24 tokens left and system-facts budget lines are checked by system_facts_budgets_match_computed, so avoiding a new set keeps them unchanged.

rejected.why: Needs a system-facts budget line and a headroom_rows row and test updates for no benefit.

decisions.choice: The follow-up is queued as a request on REQUEST_CHANNEL through StewardRequest::new and the same commit path as RequestQueue. For retry_on_new_code the code, not the model, sets the title to `Try again on <last job of the line>`.
decisions.reason: StewardRequest::new already checks that the text parses for athena plan. retry_reference (reading.rs:1881) reads `try again on <job>`, so a retry follow-up joins the line through the existing link and a corrected request does not.

rejected.option: Let the model write the whole request text
rejected.why: It could omit the link or acceptance and be refused by athena plan.

decisions.choice: No refusal, parser or matching rule is added or changed. group_lines, retry_reference and the T1-T5 thresholds are untouched.
decisions.reason: The refusal-corpus instruction applies to input-form rules. This change adds a count over existing attempt verdicts and a schema check on model output.

risks.risk: At two failures the scope guard usually flags (T1 needs the next attempt to be the 3rd) or pauses (T4), so the existing flagged or paused exit would win and no diagnosis would be queued.
risks.mitigation: Run diagnosis_end at the top of every attempt and at the failures >= ATTEMPTS exit; run it before paused_reason and flagged_reason. Tests cover a fresh line with two failures in one run, a line with a prior failure, and a second drain run.

risks.risk: Two drain workers, or two drain runs, diagnose the same line twice.
risks.mitigation: Mark creation uses OpenOptions::create_new; a second caller gets an error and queues nothing. A test calls diagnose_line twice. The drain also checks standing.diagnosis before calling diagnose.

risks.risk: A role failure leaves a claimed line with no follow-up, or an automatic re-run spends again.
risks.mitigation: The claim is written before the model call; failure records the error in the mark and queues nothing. Status shows `diagnosis failed`; deleting the file (path in the message) allows a new try. A test covers invalid output.

risks.risk: The follow-up is committed but the mark is not completed (crash between the two), so the line would look undiagnosed.
risks.mitigation: The follow-up request is committed in the same records commit as the invocation record and the mark is completed right after. If the process dies in between, the mark reads `claimed, no follow-up`, which status shows. Documented in the diagnosis.rs doc comment.

risks.risk: The retry follow-up joins the same line, which has 2 failures, and the drain would block it or retry it without bound.
risks.mitigation: The drain runs a diagnosed line's own follow-up only while no attempt has failed since the diagnosis (mark stores failed count at diagnosis), and passes everything else over. Test: follow-up item runs once and is not retried after it fails.

risks.risk: The diagnosis mark is local, so another machine's drain would diagnose the same line again.
risks.mitigation: The mark file lives in the local state directory, like pause and flag marks, and the committed follow-up request and invocation record carry the result. Stated in the CHANGELOG entry and the diagnosis.rs doc.

risks.risk: Records validation may refuse an invocation record added to a job that already has an outcome.
risks.mitigation: Run the end-to-end diagnose_line test through the real commit path and Records::load. If a closed job's directory rejects a new invocation record, file it under a fresh job id like the steward run instead and route it in store.rs.

risks.risk: Adding a field to Job, which denies unknown fields, breaks old readers or struct literals.
risks.mitigation: Make `line` optional and default-skipped, as for `pin`, so old records load. Update the Job literals the compiler reports (store.rs, reading.rs, records.rs tests). Records written by this build are not read by an older binary because Job denies unknown fields; the same holds for earlier optional fields.

risks.risk: The schema attribute for exactly one follow-up may not be supported by the schemars version in use, or the frame and enum ids may drift apart.
risks.mitigation: The frame states the output field names and ids; DiagnosisOutput::check is authoritative (the schema length bound is advisory, and the check test covers zero and two follow-ups). The test draws the ids from the enums' ALL constants.

risks.risk: The new frame exceeds the 1300-token budget set it is checked against.
risks.mitigation: Keep the frame short; the lib.rs test checks the composed size against the verifier budget before any other work depends on it.

demonstrations.method: Integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs with the existing Stub. Case A: Stub says the line already has 1 failed attempt, and the first run in this drain is rejected. Case B: a fresh line whose two runs are both rejected. Case C: after A, call drain::drain again on the same Stub. Assert the exact log, that `diagnose` was called exactly once in total, that no `reread`/`run a-retry` follows the second failure, and that the item is reported as passed over with the diagnosis reason.
demonstrations.observes: Log is [read a, run a, diagnose a] for A and [read a, run a, reread a, run a-retry, diagnose a] for B. After the second drain the log has no new run entries and the diagnose count is still 1.

A drain with the line at two failures keeps retrying or ends as plain `failed twice`. The re-run case would also call diagnose a second time if the drain ignored the standing's diagnosis.
